answer: An agent's identity accumulates age-weight only through sustained proof-of-work: each verified action burns compute whose receipt is chained into the next, so a fresh sybil starts at zero and must replicate the entire history to borrow credibility. Like tending an orchard, trust grows per season of real labor, not per seed bought. To spin up N credible identities, an attacker pays N times the full aging cost, while honest agents pay once. A nebula of young clones stays dim; only long-burning ember accounts reach voting quorum.
